findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into raw-HTML post (stored XSS)
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` appends `#{url}` to the contents without any HTML escaping, and the resulting post is stored with `cook_method = raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim and it is rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed view and as `cooked` on the main site. The `url` comes from the user-controlled `embed_url` query parameter (via `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` -> `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` -> `import_remote`); only the host is validated, the path is attacker-controlled and URI parsing permits `'`. A URL such as `http:///x'onmouseover='alert(1)` breaks out of the href attribute and Nokogiri's `absolutize_urls` round-trip preserves the injected attribute. Escape `url` (e.g. `ERB::Util.html_escape`) or build the anchor with Nokogiri.

findings.title: Any unauthenticated visitor can create unlimited topics by varying embed_url
findings.body: `EmbedController#best` enqueues `RetrieveTopic` for any `embed_url` that has no existing `TopicEmbed`. `TopicRetriever` only checks that the URL's host equals `embeddable_host` and throttles per exact URL (60s). An attacker who can set the Referer (or simply a visitor of the embedding site) can request `embed/best?embed_url=http://host/page?x=1`, `?x=2`, ... each of which passes the host check, triggers an outbound HTTP fetch of the page (plus a full RSS poll if enabled), and creates a brand new topic and post as `embed_by_username` because `import_remote` imports whatever 200 response comes back. This allows unbounded topic spam and outbound request amplification from unauthenticated requests. The URL should be normalized (strip query/fragment) and ideally only created when it appears in the feed or a per-host rate limit should be applied.

findings.title: import_remote relies on open-uri being loaded elsewhere
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on an http URL but `topic_embed.rb` never requires `open-uri`; the only `require 'open-uri'` is in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`. When autoloading (development, or any process where `Jobs::PollFeed` has not been referenced, e.g. `feed_polling_enabled` is false so `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` never touches it), `Kernel#open` treats the URL as a filename and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so embeds are never retrieved. Add `require 'open-uri'` in `topic_embed.rb` (and preferably use an explicit HTTP client rather than `Kernel#open`, which also executes shell commands for strings beginning with `|`).

findings.title: `i.content.scrub` fails on RSS items and on Ruby < 2.1
findings.body: SimpleRSS items only populate `content` for Atom feeds (RSS 2.0 items use `description`), so `i.content` is frequently `nil` and `nil.scrub` raises `NoMethodError`, aborting the whole poll (the job also has `retry: false`). Additionally `String#scrub` was added in Ruby 2.1; on the Ruby 2.0 this codebase targets it does not exist. Use `i.content || i.description` with a nil guard and avoid `scrub` or add a fallback. There is also no per-item rescue, so one bad item prevents importing all others.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` is a malformed ERB block terminator
findings.body: The header `if/else` block is closed with `<%- end if %>`. Ruby treats the trailing `if` as a statement modifier and, because a newline after `if` is permitted, consumes the next generated buffer-append statement as its condition. The template only works by accident (the append expression is truthy) and any change to the following markup can turn this into a syntax error or silently skip the `end`. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Success spec mocks TopicView.new with a nil return, so the best template cannot render
findings.body: `TopicView.expects(:new).with(123, nil, {best: 5})` has no `returns`, so `@topic_view` is nil and `best.html.erb` calls `@topic_view.posts` on nil. The `after` hook asserts `response.should be_success`, so either this spec fails or the view is not actually being exercised. Return a stubbed topic view (with `posts` and `topic`) so the template, including the `end if` block and the header/footer branches, is genuinely rendered and verified.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to wrong absolute URLs
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` treats every href/src starting with `/` as site-relative and strips all leading slashes, so a protocol-relative URL like `//cdn.example.com/img.png` becomes `http://<host>/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking images and links. Check for `start_with?('//')` and prefix only the scheme (or leave such URLs alone).

findings.title: setnx/expire throttle is not atomic; key can become permanent
findings.body: `retrieved_recently?` does `$redis.setnx` and then a separate `$redis.expire`. If the process dies or the connection drops between the two calls, the `retrieved:<url>` key is left with no TTL and that URL is permanently throttled for non-staff users, so the embed never loads. Use a single atomic `SET key 1 NX EX 60` (or a MULTI block).

findings.title: Failed PostCreator result treated as success
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` returns the `Post` object even when creation was rolled back (e.g. host-spam detection), in which case the post is unsaved with errors. `post.present?` is true for such an object, so `TopicEmbed.create!` is attempted with `post_id: nil`/`topic_id: nil` and raises `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid`, and `import` returns an unsaved post to callers. Check `post.errors.blank? && post.persisted?` instead.

findings.title: Origin check uses substring match
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`, e.g. an origin `http://forum.example.co` passes when `discourseUrl` is `http://forum.example.com/`. Impact is limited to iframe height manipulation, but the check should compare `e.origin` with the exact origin derived from `discourseUrl`.
